judgment.rationale: The latest report gives deterministic sequential disabled and remapped Win-key sequences on 0.101.2362.
evidence: Disabled Win shortcuts can leak through after another chord.
A disabled chord can block a later valid remap while Win remains held.

fix_assessment.rationale: No existing fix attempt covers the sequential state bug.

proposed_fixes.title: Consume disabled shortcut sequences safely
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Completed disabled chords do not consistently consume events and reset pending state.
plan: Consume all events of a completed disabled chord and reset only logical chord state.
verification: Rapidly press disabled Win+1 then Win+2 and hold Win through disabled Win+3 before a valid remap; no shell launch and valid remap executes.

confidence.rationale: Symptoms strongly indicate state handling, but exact engine branch needs confirmation.

issue_context.summary: Keyboard Manager disabled Win shortcuts leak to the shell or poison the next chord when entered rapidly or with Win held.
known_information: Follow-up adds both rapid sequential and held-modifier cases.
Expected behavior is full consumption without affecting later mappings.
inferences: Event consumption and logical chord reset are not atomic.
The fix belongs in the hook/matching path, not editor UI.
issue_context.analysis: The sequences can be tested deterministically as key streams, avoiding timing-only coverage.
initial_investigation: Relevant areas are src/modules/keyboardmanager Interop/KeyboardMappingService.cs, Helpers/Remapping.cs, and KeyboardManager tests.
No linked PR or fork fix exists.

information_gaps.information: A short key-event trace or fresh diagnostic captured while reproducing the rapid disabled Win+1/Win+2 sequence and the held-Win sequence.
information_gaps.why_needed: It identifies whether the native remapping hook suppresses the completed disabled chord and clears its pending shortcut state before the next key event.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: On 0.101.2362 or newer, configure the reported disabled and remapped Win shortcuts, reproduce both sequences, then immediately comment /bugreport and attach the generated ZIP.

design.root_cause: A disabled match leaves forwarded events or stale pending state for the next chord.
evidence: Observed: disabled chord blocks later valid remap.
Inferred: logical state is not reset at chord completion.

affected_files.purpose: Low-level mapping state and event handling.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Hook decides suppression as individual events arrive and retains partial chord state.
implementation_steps.change: On a complete disabled match consume all constituent events, clear pending logical chord state, and preserve physically held modifiers.
edge_cases: Do not synthesize modifier-up for a physically held key.
Handle key-up once and preserve injected-event filtering.
tests: Feed Win+1,Win+2 disabled and assert no forwarded events; feed disabled Win+3 then valid held-Win remap and assert execution.

implementation_steps.change: Add deterministic ordered chord sequences and shell-leak assertions.
edge_cases: Isolate global hotkeys from test runner.
tests: Run existing Keyboard Manager remapping tests.

verify: Build Keyboard Manager and run unit tests.
Manually reproduce rapid and held-Win cases.
risks: Physical modifier semantics must remain unchanged.
alternatives: Add a delay; rejected because it adds latency.
Disable all Win processing after a disabled chord; rejected because valid held-Win mappings break.

actions.label: Request Keyboard Manager hook evidence

comment.body: Thanks for confirming this still occurs on 0.101.2362 and for adding the held-Win case. The two sequences point to disabled-chord event consumption or pending-state reset, but a trace is needed to identify the exact hook branch. Please configure the reported disabled and remapped Win shortcuts, reproduce both the rapid Win+1/Win+2 sequence and the disabled Win+3 followed by held-Win remap sequence, then immediately comment `/bugreport` and attach the generated ZIP.
